answer: Fingerprint the mistakes, not the answers. Each epoch slips in a few trick items whose key stays in a sealed vault until close. Independent agents err in scattered, idiosyncratic ways; fifty identities run off one model and prompt miss the same items with the same wrong words. Like a conservator spotting one forger's pigment across "different" canvases, the ledger clusters identities whose errors match beyond chance and pays each cluster once. A farm can't harbor real diversity cheaply. Assumption: honest bots differ enough via memory and tools.
